speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: It's tea, strong and bitter and unapproved. Drink it while it's still three things the Ministry dislikes.
after: It's tea. Strong, bitter, unapproved. Finish the cup.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: It began the night the boy got out, they say. Nobody says 'boy' where the loudspeakers can hear.
after: It began the night the boy got out, they say. Don't say 'boy' near a loudspeaker.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Keep your voice down, will you? I'm Old Fern. Composter, which in this city is about the worst thing a person can be.
after: Keep your voice down, will you? I'm Old Fern, and I'm a composter, which in this city is about the worst thing a body can own up to.

speaker: Old Fern
before: I spent forty years turning this city's scraps back into soil, and now that's 'untidy'. So am I, apparently. I've got worms in my hat to prove it.
after: Forty years I turned this city's scraps back into good soil, and then one morning it was all 'untidy', and so was I. Well, I've got worms in my hat, so I suppose they had a point.

speaker: Old Fern
before: They swept the rubbish behind the facade and pretended it wasn't there. Now the soil's sick, nothing grows in the Reek, and I'm too old to dig alone. Help me save what's left.
after: They swept the rubbish in behind the facade and called that clean. Now the soil's sick and nothing grows in the Reek, and my knees won't do the digging alone any more. Help me save what's left of it.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Any luck? The heaps are tucked into cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding from the inspectors. Tell them they're coming home.
after: Well, any luck? My heaps are tucked down cellars and holes all over the Reek, keeping quiet because they think the inspectors are still after them. You tell them from me that they're coming home.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Oh, you've come to the door. Forgive me, it's been a long while since anyone did. I'm Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.
after: Oh, you've come to the door. Forgive me, it's been such a long while since anyone did. I'm Widow Pell, and my husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: I still talk to him in there. He was always the patient one of us, and it turns out I'm not. If you can help at all, please.
after: I still go in and talk to him, I'm afraid. He's always been the patient one of the two of us, and I'm finding that I am not. I'm sorry to ask it of a stranger, but if you could help us at all...

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where no official would ever look: in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads.
after: I'm told somebody kind hid the Stamp of Final Approval where no official would ever think to look: in Grave Row, north of the permit office, in among papers nobody reads. I'm only sorry I can't go myself.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Name's Rollo Spokes... wheel foreman, Beefcake, out of the Gainlands. Back home... a wheel stopped at night... and so did the man on it.
after: Give me a second... Rollo Spokes. I'm a wheel foreman, a Beefcake out of the Gainlands. Back home, when a wheel stopped for the night... the man on it stopped too, and went home to his supper.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Here, the facade needs lighting... so we pedal it. No pay, no end. They told us it was cardio... My calves have calves.
after: Here the facade wants lighting day and night... so we pedal it, with no pay and no end of shift. They told us it was cardio... and I'll say this much for it, my calves have grown calves.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Three wheels in the Yards... pull each brake and talk to the crew. Then the big cable by the east wall, the one that feeds the facade... cut it.
after: There's three wheels in the Yards... pull the brake on each one and have a word with the crew. After that it's the big cable by the east wall, the one that feeds the facade... you cut that.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: The crews won't get off... till somebody tells them it's all right to. So you tell them... and mean it.
after: They won't climb down off those wheels... not till somebody tells them it's all right to. So you tell them... and you mean it when you do, because they'll know if you don't.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Hands where I can see them... good, no inspector's gloves. I'm Chef Marlo. I cooked at the Market of the Four Paths, once. Now I'm a 'Nutrient Distributor', and my recipes stay in my apron.
after: Hands where I can see them first... good, no inspector's gloves. I'm Chef Marlo. I used to cook at the Market of the Four Paths, and now they call me a 'Nutrient Distributor' and my recipes live in my apron.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste, three times a day. Paste is food the way a form is a hug.
after: Everybody in this city eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste three times a day, and between you and me, paste is food the way a form is a hug.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: For ten years I've hidden real recipes all over this quarter, so that somebody, somewhere, remembers what food is.
after: So for ten years I've been tucking real recipes away in corners all over this quarter, so that somebody, somewhere, will still remember what food is when all this is over.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Three recipe cards, tucked away around the quarter, and then the dispenser. Spoil it for me, and spoil it badly. I've waited ten years to say that.
after: Keep it down. It's three recipe cards, tucked away around the quarter, and after that the paste dispenser. Spoil it for me, and spoil it properly, because I've waited ten years to say that to somebody.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: HALT. I am Captain Spotless. State your height.
after: HALT! I am Captain Spotless, and this gate is mine to keep clean. State your height.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: No: do not state it. Stand at it. Straighter. Not that straight. APPROVED straight.
after: No: do not state it. Stand at it. Straighter than that, but not as straight as THAT, which is showing off. Stand APPROVED straight.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are somehow both too tall and too short, and your shadow is the wrong length.
after: Entry to the Capital requires the Approved Visitor Standard, and you do not meet it. You are somehow both too tall and too short, and your shadow is the wrong length for the hour.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: However, the Standard provides for an Entry Examination, conducted as a card battle. Win it, and you are retroactively approved.
after: The Standard does, however, provide for an Entry Examination, which is conducted as a card battle. Should you win it, you will be retroactively approved, and I shall have to sign for you.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: Do not look nervous. Nervousness is a Violation. (He polishes a button.) Shall we begin?
after: And do not look nervous, because nervousness is a Violation under the same Standard. (He polishes a button.) Shall we begin?

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: You again. Still too tall. Still smiling at the wrong angle. Ready for the Examination?
after: You again, and I see that you are still too tall and still smiling at the wrong angle. Are you ready to sit the Examination?

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: You are approved. I have always supported this outcome. Please remember that exact wording.
after: You are approved, and I should like it noted that I have always supported this outcome. Please remember that exact wording, in case anybody asks.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: Please do not tell {villain_title} that I lost. Please do not tell anyone that I lost.
after: And please do not tell {villain_title} that I lost. In fact, if it is all the same to you, please do not tell anyone at all.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: You are... approved. You are retroactively approved.
after: You are... approved. Let the record show that you are retroactively approved, as of some time before I lost.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: I have measured twelve thousand visitors and approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. About the rest, I would rather not say.
after: In my years at this gate I have measured twelve thousand visitors and approved four. Nine thousand were sent home, and about the rest I would rather not say.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: Go through, citizen. In there, try not to be what you are.
after: Go through, citizen, and for your own sake, once you are in there, try not to be what you are.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: I am Citizen 4471. I was brought here for smiling incorrectly. Eleven degrees, when the approved angle is eight.
after: Good day! I am Citizen 4471, and I am being helped. I was brought here for smiling incorrectly: eleven degrees, when the approved angle is eight.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: It was our wedding day. I had been crying, the happy kind, and they corrected me for that too.
after: It was... it was our wedding day, you see. I had been crying, the happy kind of crying, and they corrected me for that as well.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: I am improving, they say. I am not sure that is a good thing.
after: They tell me I am improving, and I thank them for it. ...Between ourselves, I am not at all sure that it is a good thing.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: All we want is a burial permit: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval, and then he can finally rest.
after: All we're asking for is a burial permit, you see. It's Form 27-B/6, and it only wants the Stamp of Final Approval on it, and then he can stop waiting in that chair and rest at last.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. Find it, take it to our family plot at the north end of the Row, and let him rest.
after: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. If you would find it and carry it to our family plot at the north end of the Row, he could lie down at last.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: The stamp's in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. Then bring it to our plot at the north end of the Row. Please.
after: I'm sorry to keep on at you. The stamp is in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among the papers nobody reads, and when you have it, it wants taking to our plot at the north end of the Row.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: He's at rest? Oh. Oh.
after: He's at rest? Truly? Oh... oh, forgive me, I shall need a moment.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: I sat by the plot all morning and didn't say a word. It was the first quiet in three years that wasn't a fear.
after: I sat by the plot the whole morning and never said a word to him, and it was the first quiet in three years that I wasn't afraid of.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Here, this was his. He'd want it to go to someone young, who'll use it.
after: Here, please take this. It was his, and he'd want it to go to somebody young who will get some use out of it, and not leave it sitting in a drawer.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: There's something you should know about the man in the castle. He schedules grief: Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.
after: There is one thing you ought to know about the man in the castle. He has grief on a schedule: Thursdays, from 3:00 to 3:05, and anyone found crying outside those five minutes is corrected.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Thank you, a hundred times over. I sit with him at the plot every morning now. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he can't bear a sadness he didn't schedule.
after: Thank you, a hundred times over. I sit with him at the plot every morning now, and nobody moves me along. Do remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he can't bear a sadness he didn't schedule.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull each brake lever... and tell them it's all right, in plain words.
after: There's three wheels in the Transit Yards... and three crews on them that nobody ever told to stop. Pull the brake lever on each one... and tell them it's all right, in plain words they can't mishear.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: They won't believe you at first... say it anyway. Then cut the big cable by the east wall. Those facade lights have run on my crews' legs... for ten years.
after: They won't believe you the first time... so you say it again. Then go and cut the big cable by the east wall. Those facade lights have been running on my crews' legs... for ten years now.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews, then cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop... it takes a few goes.
after: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... get the crews off them, then cut the big cable by the east wall. And keep on telling them they can stop... it takes a few goes before it sinks in.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: I heard the lights flicker from here... then I heard the crews sit down. The whole yard's gone quiet.
after: I heard the lights flicker from all the way over here... and then I heard my crews sit down, one wheel after another. The whole yard's gone quiet.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Haven't heard a quiet yard since the coup. Thank you.
after: I haven't heard a yard go quiet since the coup... and I'd forgotten how much I liked it. Thank you.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Here... from the old days. We gave these out... at the end of a shift. Remember ends?
after: Here, take this... it's from the old days. We used to hand these out at the end of a shift... back when a shift had an end to it.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: One more thing about the man in the castle: he made lateness illegal. That's a man who can't bear to wait for anyone.
after: One more thing, about the man in the castle... he made lateness illegal. Now what sort of man does that? One who can't bear to wait for anybody, that's who.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: The wheels are slowing... and the crews are resting. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement... and that's the one thing he won't forgive.
after: The wheels are slowing down... and the crews are getting some rest at last. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement... and that's the one thing he won't forgive.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Three of my recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter: a bread, a stew, a sauce. Real ones, in my hand, quantities written as 'some'. Find them before the inspectors do.
after: There's three of my recipes hidden in the Hungry Quarter: a bread, a stew and a sauce. They're real ones, in my own hand, with the quantities written as 'some'. Find them before the inspectors do, will you?

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: And the paste dispenser here in the quarter: spoil it for me. Put something in it that tastes of something.
after: And then there's the paste dispenser, here in the quarter. I want you to spoil it for me. Get something into it that actually tastes of something, and I don't much mind what.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. You'll know my cards: 'some' of this, 'a bit' of that. That's how a good recipe reads.
after: It's three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and then the dispenser to spoil. You'll know my cards when you see them: 'some' of this and 'a bit' of that, which is how any honest recipe ought to read.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: The bread! The stew! The sauce!
after: The bread, and the stew, and... you found the sauce as well? Give them here, quick, before somebody sees!

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Look at the stains on them, look at the spelling! And that smell from the dispenser... cabbage. Real cabbage.
after: Look at the stains on them, and look at my spelling, it's dreadful! And that smell coming off the dispenser... that's cabbage, isn't it? Real boiled cabbage, stinking up the whole street.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: I'm crying, and you'll let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.
after: Yes, I'm crying, and you'll just have to let me. Here, this is for you: my real recipe, the one I never once dared to write down until today.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: And one thing about the man in the castle: he can't taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.
after: And I'll tell you one thing about the man in the castle that not many people know: he can't taste. Not his food, not his wine, not even salt, and he never could.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: He built a whole kingdom of paste because he could not understand what the rest of us were missing.
after: So he went and built a whole kingdom of paste, because he honestly could not understand what the rest of us thought we were missing.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: I'm cooking again, real food with a real mess. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he made everyone eat what he couldn't taste.
after: I'm cooking again, real food, and making a real mess while I do it. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he made everyone eat what he couldn't taste.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and yards and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive, whatever the inspectors say.
after: There's three compost heaps hiding in the Reek, down in cellars and yards and under floors, where they were told to wait. I want them rescued. They're alive, whatever the inspectors like to say about it.

speaker: Old Fern
before: And there's a jar of old seed somewhere in the Reek. Plant it in the Sick Patch. Nobody's planted a thing in this city for ten years.
after: And somewhere in the Reek there's a jar of old seed. Find it and plant it in the Sick Patch for me, because nobody's put a thing in the ground in this city for ten years and it's high time somebody did.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Three heaps to rescue in the Reek, and the seed for the Sick Patch. Find the jar first, then give the seed its chance. It's waited long enough.
after: That's three heaps to rescue in the Reek, and the seed for the Sick Patch. Find the jar first, mind, and then give that seed its chance. It's waited long enough, and so have I.

speaker: Old Fern
before: It took? It TOOK! A flower, in this city, after all this time.
after: It took? You're telling me it TOOK? A flower, a real one, in this city, after all this time!

speaker: Old Fern
before: I need to sit down. I need to sit down and smell it.
after: I'm going to have to sit down. I'm going to sit right down in the dirt beside it and smell it, and you can think what you like.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Here, take this. And one thing about the man in the castle: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.
after: Here, take this, you've earned it. And I'll tell you one thing about the man in the castle: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Weeds, moss, children. Anything that might surprise him. I reckon that's the whole of him.
after: Weeds, moss, children. Anything at all that might surprise him. I've had a good while to think about it, out here with the worms, and I reckon that's the whole of him.

speaker: Old Fern
before: The patch is blooming and the heaps are steaming, untidy as you like. Remember what I said, it's in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.
after: The patch is blooming and the heaps are steaming, and it's all as untidy as you like. Remember what I said, it's in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: The dispenser's spoiled, and lovely it is too. But the paste has to come from somewhere, doesn't it?
after: The dispenser's spoiled, and a lovely job you made of it too. But I've been lying awake over it, because all that paste has to be coming from somewhere, doesn't it?

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: The shuttered stall at the quarter's south-west corner hums at night, and stalls don't hum. Open its ration hatch and have a look down. Gently.
after: There's a shuttered stall at the Hungry Quarter's south-west corner that hums at night, and I've worked stalls all my life and never met one that hummed. Open its ration hatch and have a look down. Go gently.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: It's the south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch, go down, and shut off whatever you find. I'd bet it's very, very grey.
after: It's the stall at the south-west corner, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch, climb down, and shut off whatever you find at the bottom. I'd bet my apron it's very, very grey.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: You shut the vats down? All of them? Then tonight the whole quarter eats something that tastes of something.
after: You shut the vats down? Every last one of them? Then tonight, for the first time in ten years, this whole quarter sits down to something that tastes of something.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Some taste. 'Some' is the best amount.
after: It won't be much taste to begin with, only some. But I've always said that 'some' is the best amount.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and twelve minutes. I have had the figure framed.
after: You again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and twelve minutes, and I have had that figure framed so that I am obliged to look at it.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: These wheels lit the facade at a hundred and ten percent. Now they are 'resting'. Do you know what rest is? Unmeasured time.
after: These wheels lit the facade at a hundred and ten percent of capacity, and now their crews are 'resting'. Do you know what rest is? It is time that nobody has measured.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: They're allowed to stop.
after: They've been on those wheels for ten years, and they're allowed to stop.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Nobody is allowed anything. People are scheduled. Let me schedule you.
after: Nobody is allowed anything. People are scheduled, and I find that I have an opening of roughly ninety seconds. Let me schedule you.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Eighty-one seconds. Faster than last time. You have improved by fourteen percent.
after: Eighty-one seconds, which is faster than last time. You have improved by fourteen percent.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: The crews voted... while you two were busy. You're staying put... till Flex's people come down. Some of those wheels... had children on them. They'd like a word.
after: The crews took a vote... while you two were busy. You're staying right here, Minister... till Flex's people come down for you. Some of those wheels had children on them... They'd like a word.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Detained. I have never been detained. I do not even know how long it takes.
after: Detained? I have never been detained before, and I do not even know how long it is supposed to take.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: I will find out. I will time every minute of it.
after: I will find out, of course. I intend to time every minute of it.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now, the lawns and the hedges both. They grow in whatever direction they please.
after: An inch out of regulation. I'm afraid everything is out of regulation now, the lawns and the hedges alike, and they have all begun growing in whatever direction they please.

speaker: Old Fern
before: That's what hedges DO.
after: That's what hedges DO, woman! It's the whole point of a hedge!

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Nothing grew there for ten years.
after: I've stood in her valley. Nothing grew there for ten years.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump, sorting peel from shell all day long. It's messy work, and you'd hate it. Good. It's yours if you want it.
after: Granny Gristle wants hands on the compost rows down in the Dump, sorting peel from shell all day long. It's filthy work and you'd hate every minute, which is why I thought of you. It's yours if you want it.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: And you must be the volunteer. A Certificate of Participation. Frame it, or don't. It's been notarized either way.
after: And you must be our brave volunteer! Do accept this Certificate of Participation. Frame it or don't, as the mood takes you; it has been notarized either way!

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: That's Percival Plume, dear. Deputy Minister of Good News. He drafted the transfer. Every page of it.
after: That's Percival Plume, dear, the Deputy Minister of Good News. He's the one who drafted the transfer that signed us all over, and he wrote every page of it himself.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: And had a clerk file it, on a Tuesday, I believe! Must dash. Ribbons to cut, a Capital to reassure. Toodle-oo!
after: And had a clerk file it, on a Tuesday, I believe! Well, I really must dash: there are ribbons to cut and a Capital to reassure. Toodle-oo!

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Just measuring. There's a lot of very tidy people in this city, and tidy is easy to measure.
after: Just measuring, same as ever. There's a great many very tidy people in this city, mind, and I will say that tidy is lovely and easy to measure.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Him? Hm.
after: Him? Hm. Let me have a look in the book.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Just measuring. Ran into a peacock earlier, all trumpet and ribbons.
after: Just measuring. I ran into a peacock earlier, mind, all trumpet and ribbons, and he never so much as stopped to say good morning.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Oh, I've got HIM in pen. Heh. Not soon, mind. I just wanted it to last.
after: Oh, I've got HIM in pen. Not soon, mind, so there's no call to look at me like that. I just like to have one or two of them settled. Heh.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: HALT. That is a smudge. That is a smudge on a CITIZEN.
after: HALT! That is a smudge, and what is worse, it is a smudge on a CITIZEN!

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: HALT. Stand at attention. No: at THAT attention.
after: HALT! Stand at attention. No, not at your own attention: at THAT attention!

speaker: Vivienne Quota
before: Two-minute break. Mandatory. I wrote the schedule. I resent the schedule.
after: A two-minute break is now mandatory. I wrote that schedule myself, and I resent it.

speaker: Kestrel
before: Psst. Down. The enforcers walk this road on the hour, and they hate surprises. I'm a surprise.
after: Psst. Get down, will you? The enforcers walk this road on the hour, and they hate surprises, and I'm a surprise.

speaker: Kestrel
before: Name's Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Heading into the city? The gate's the only way in for strangers. There's an older way under it, but I only show that to friends of Wren's.
after: Name's Kestrel, and I scout for the Wrinkles, which you never heard me say. Heading into the city? The gate's the only way in for strangers. There's an older way under it, but I only show that to friends of Wren's.

speaker: Kestrel
before: Road's clear for ten minutes. Chalk's fresh. Move while the guards are busy being punctual somewhere else.
after: Road's clear for ten minutes, and the chalk's fresh, so I'd know. Go on, move, while the guards are busy being punctual somewhere else, and try not to walk so much like a stranger.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: ATTENTION! You are standing in a restricted pantry, soldier! Every recipe on those shelves has been confiscated for the war effort!
after: ATTENTION! You are standing in a restricted pantry, soldier, and every recipe on those shelves has been confiscated for the war effort!

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Which war? The war on FLAVOUR, son! Every citizen fed the same ration, at the same minute, from the same tap, and not one complaint about the seasoning.
after: Which war, you ask? The war on FLAVOUR, soldier! Every citizen fed the same ration, at the same minute, from the same tap, and I have not had one complaint about the seasoning in ten years!

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Taste is a weakness, soldier, and I have none! Golems, whisk formation, to the vats! Nobody touches my pantry!
after: Taste is a weakness, soldier, and I am proud to say I have none! Golems, whisk formation, and to the vats with you! Nobody lays a finger on my pantry!

id: data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense/line::0
speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Ration line, ATTENTION! Whisk formation! Nobody tastes anything!
after: Ration line, ATTENTION! Fall in by whisk formation, and nobody is to taste ANYTHING!

speaker: Enforcer Captain Spotless
before: INSPECTION. Height! Smudges! Smiles at the regulation angle!
after: INSPECTION! I want heights, I want smudges, and I want every smile at the regulation angle!

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Stand down. Stand DOWN. I said... oh, everyone's already lying down. Very well.
after: Stand down! Stand DOWN, I said... oh. I see that everyone is already lying down. Very well, carry on lying.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Then you'll learn again. The Grand Chef is taking students, and she starts every one of them the same way: first, water.
after: Then you'll just have to learn it again, same as a boy on his first day. The Grand Chef is taking students, and she starts every one of them the same way: first, water.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You copied my cards. You can't copy what I do with them.
after: You copied my cards, but you can't copy what I do with them.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You copied my cards. You can't copy what I do with them.
after: You copied my cards, but you can't copy what I do with them.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Ah! You found my memo. Isn't it well written? I used the active voice.
after: Ah, you found my memo! Isn't it beautifully written? I used the active voice throughout, which I am told is very daring in a memo.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News. I drafted the transfer of the D.N.A., notarized it, had a clerk file it, and read it out on every loudspeaker in the land.
after: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News, at your service! I drafted the transfer of the D.N.A., notarized it, had a clerk file it, and read it out on every loudspeaker in the land!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Beneath the forest where you... oh, I shouldn't have said that. Never mind. Great news: your visit is being declined!
after: Why, beneath the forest where you... oh. Oh, I really shouldn't have said that, should I? Never mind! Great news: your visit is being declined, effective immediately!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: I'll draft a statement. 'Minister Plume bravely withdrew.' Yes. Bravely.
after: I shall draft a statement at once: 'Minister Plume bravely withdrew.' Yes, I like that. Bravely is exactly the word.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Old Fern, composter, and I'm allowed to say so out loud now.
after: Old Fern, composter, and I'll say it as loud as I please now, so don't you go shushing me.

speaker: Old Fern
before: The patch came in, the heaps are steaming, and nobody's thumped me for it in a week. I'm untidy, and I'm proud of it.
after: The patch came in, the heaps are steaming, and nobody's thumped me for any of it in a week. I'm untidy and I always was, and these days I'm proud of it.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry, but it'd be a waste of good water. Come back any time.
after: Smell that? That's honest compost, that is. I could cry over it, but it'd be a waste of good water, so I'll just stand here and breathe. You come back any time you like.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: I'm Widow Pell. My husband is finally at rest, and I visit him every morning, the way I always meant to.
after: I'm Widow Pell, and I'm so glad you've come by. My husband is at rest at last, and I walk up to visit him every morning, the way I always meant to.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Thank you. I will never say it enough, so I keep saying it.
after: Thank you. I know I shall never manage to say it enough, so you'll have to forgive me if I simply keep on saying it.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: We're well. My husband would have said you were late. He'd have meant it fondly.
after: We're both very well, thank you for asking. My husband says you're late, mind you, but he only ever says that to people he's fond of.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Rollo Spokes. The wheels are slow, and the crews are sitting in the sun, lifting nothing. Best I've ever seen them look.
after: Rollo Spokes... and look at that, I've nearly got my breath back. The wheels are turning slow and the crews are sat out in the sun, lifting nothing at all... and it's the best I've ever seen them look.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: We're lifting again, real things and on purpose this time. Come and watch the crews, and bring a snack.
after: We're lifting again... real things, and on purpose this time, because we feel like it. Come down and watch the crews some afternoon... and bring a snack, they'll want to share theirs.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Chef Marlo. Chef. Say it with me. The stalls are open and the food is real.
after: It's Chef Marlo. Chef! Go on, say it with me, I can't hear it often enough. The stalls are open and every single thing on them is real food.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: And chaotic, I'll grant you. There's flour on the ceiling, and I've never been so happy to see a mess.
after: It's chaos, I'll grant you that. There's flour on the ceiling and somebody's burned the onions twice, and I have never in my life been so happy to look at a mess.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Come and eat. 'Some' of everything. If you ask how much, I shall have to demonstrate.
after: Come and eat! You're having 'some' of everything, and if you ask me how much that is, I'll have no choice but to demonstrate with the big ladle.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: I smile now, when I want to. It comes out crooked, and my wife says it's the best thing she's ever seen.
after: I smile whenever I want to now, and it comes out crooked every time. My wife says it's the best thing she's ever seen. I told her she was wrong, just to try disagreeing, and we both enjoyed it very much.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: It's Aldous. Still crooked, but I'm practising.
after: It's Aldous, remember? The smile's still crooked, but I'm practising it on everybody I meet, and so far nobody has written me up for it.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: My tea's still unapproved, but then nothing's approved any more. Best thing that ever happened to it.
after: Tea's still unapproved. So is everything else now. Suits it.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: I have filed a Form of Gratitude, dear. It was approved on the first attempt. Irregular.
after: I have filed a Form of Gratitude on your behalf, dear, and it was approved on the first attempt. That is highly irregular, and I find I rather like irregular.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: He is allowed visitors, one at a time, ten minutes, no mirrors. Those are the rules. I did not write them, and I find I do not mind them.
after: He is allowed visitors: one at a time, ten minutes each, and no mirrors. Those are the rules. I did not write them and nobody made me recite them, and I find I do not mind them at all.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: He designs very good drains, it turns out. Do not tell him I said so.
after: He designs a very good drain, as it turns out. Please do not tell him I said so; I am not sure which of us it would embarrass more.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Ah. You did it, then, the castle and all.
after: Ah, there you are. You did it, then, the castle and all, and you've come back with both boots on. Lovely.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Then I've two graves to finish properly, up in Grave Row in the city. Come by when you're ready. No rush; there never is, with me.
after: That means I've two graves to finish off properly, up in Grave Row in the city. You come by when you're ready, mind. There's no rush; there never is, with me.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Back again! Walked them all the way home, I did. Lovely evening for it.
after: Back again! I walked the pair of them all the way home, I did, and it was a lovely evening for it.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see now... you're not down for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Appointments, same as always. Let's see now... no, you're not down for a good long while. Lovely! That's what I like to see. Heh.

speaker: Isla Brannoch
before: They had us painting the same front door for eight years. Every time I asked to leave, the form came back "pending".
after: They had us painting the same front door for eight years, Dad. Every time I asked to leave, the form came back "pending", and by the end I'd stopped being surprised.

speaker: Isla Brannoch
before: I keep walking to the gate and back. Nobody stops me. I keep expecting somebody to stop me.
after: I keep walking down to the gate and back again, just because I can. Nobody stops me, and I still catch myself waiting for somebody to.

speaker: Isla Brannoch
before: Dad oiled the hinges this morning. It doesn't even lock. He just likes the sound of it opening now.
after: Dad oiled the hinges this morning, on a gate that doesn't even lock. He just likes the sound of it opening now.
